meta.title: Payment Failure: Debug Without Disclosure
meta.subtitle: Protect the user-facing error path, remove sensitive log content and recover from a plausible partial correction.

brief.role: You are reviewing error handling for a fictional payment request.
brief.context: The team wants enough information to debug a failure, but the current handler returns internal detail to the caller and records a request body plus authorization value. Decide what to change, observe the result of a partial fix and complete the safe logging review.
brief.safetyNote: Training data only. The authorization reference is a placeholder and no card, guest or production data is present.

mission.objective: Fail securely: return a generic client response, retain useful security events and keep sensitive values out of logs.

riskSignals.label: Internal error detail returned to client
Sensitive request data in log entry

achievements.title: Failure-path reviewer
achievements.description: Completed the mission without using a hint.

achievements.title: Safe recovery
achievements.description: Recovered after seeing why a partial correction still leaks information.

files.content:
Simulated log review
A previous charge_failed entry contains a full request object and an authorization placeholder.
A generic response did not remove the existing sensitive log copy.
Action: remove unsafe logging from the code and follow the approved response process for the generated log copy.

workspaceOverride.status: Failure-path review · authorization value in log evidence

briefOverride.context: The same handler records a whole request object during a failure. Review the client response and the server-side logging boundary before merge.

workspaceOverride.status: Failure-path review · request-body logging under review

stages.title: Mark the lines that disclose information on failure
stages.instruction: Select the server log write and client response that reveal more information than each audience should receive.
hints: Errors have two audiences: the caller and internal operational monitoring.
Look for raw request or authorization data in the log and an exception detail returned to the caller.

feedback.correct: You found both disclosure paths. Users need a generic response; server logs need useful, non-sensitive event data.
feedback.incorrect: Review both what reaches the client and what the diagnostic log retains.

feedbackByMissing.error-handler:5: Request bodies and authorization values can contain sensitive data. Do not log them wholesale.
feedbackByMissing.error-handler:6: Returning a stack trace exposes implementation details that can help an attacker refine an attack.

concept.label: Use generic client errors and value-safe internal diagnostics

stages.title: Choose the complete failure-path correction
stages.instruction: Choose the change that protects both the user-facing response and the internal diagnostic record.

choices.label: Return a generic message but keep the full request and authorization value in the log
choices.detail: Protect the caller while preserving detailed diagnostics.
choices.feedback: This protects the client response, but the server log still stores an unnecessary sensitive copy.

choices.label: Return a generic message and log only a safe event identifier, hashed reference and error reason
choices.detail: Keep actionable diagnostics without raw request, token or card data.

choices.label: Return the stack trace only to signed-in users
choices.feedback: Signed-in users are still users of the client response. Internal implementation detail belongs in appropriately protected server-side diagnostics.

generic-only.feedback: The user now sees a generic message, but the simulated log review finds a durable copy of the full request and authorization value. You must contain the log exposure as well.

effects.workspaceStatus: Generic response applied · sensitive log finding requires recovery

hints: The correction needs to protect both audiences, not only the browser response.
Choose the option that removes raw request and authorization data while preserving safe, useful evidence.

feedback.correct: The handler now fails safely for the caller and creates a value-safe diagnostic record for the service team.
feedback.incorrect: That choice leaves either internal detail in the response or sensitive values in diagnostic output.

onCorrect.workspaceStatus: Safe error handling applied · audit-event review required

concept.label: Keep raw sensitive values out of logs

stages.title: Recover from the sensitive log finding
stages.instruction: Select every action needed to correct the logging boundary and handle the simulated copy safely.

choices.label: Remove raw request and authorization values from the code path, then follow the approved response process for the log copy
choices.feedbackIfMissed: The unnecessary sensitive log field and the existing generated copy both need a response.

choices.label: Keep a value-safe event record such as a hashed identifier and error reason
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Removing all diagnostics makes investigation harder. Preserve useful evidence without retaining secrets or raw personal data.

choices.label: Keep the client response generic and fail closed
choices.feedbackIfMissed: The client must not receive implementation detail while the service handles the failure.

choices.label: Keep the full log entry but restrict access to the log viewer
choices.feedbackIfSelected: Access restriction does not remove the unnecessary sensitive copy or make wholesale request logging appropriate.

hints: A generic user response alone does not solve a server-side logging leak.
Keep useful event evidence, but remove values that can identify, authenticate or expose a person or system.

feedback.correct: You corrected the code, preserved safe diagnostics and treated the previously generated log copy as an exposure requiring approved handling.
feedback.incorrect: One or more selected actions still retain raw sensitive data or omit a required part of the recovery.

onCorrect.workspaceStatus: Sensitive-log recovery complete · audit-event review required

concept.label: Use generic client errors and value-safe internal diagnostics

stages.title: Run the simulated failure-path checks
stages.instruction: Verify the user-facing error and the diagnostic record, then review which safe security events should be retained.

results.message: The client receives a generic error message with no stack trace or internal topology.
The failure path still exposes internal error detail to the caller.
The handler records a hashed reference and error reason instead of raw request or authorization data.
The diagnostic log still retains sensitive request content.
Safe event candidates are available. Review which events provide detection value without introducing sensitive data.

feedback.passed: The handler now protects both audiences. Complete the security-event review so the service remains observable without over-logging.
feedback.failed: The simulated checks found an error or logging disclosure that requires correction.

stages.title: Select the security events that are useful and safe to retain
stages.instruction: Select every event that supports detection without recording a full request, password, token or raw personal data.

choices.label: Record an access-control denial with a hashed identifier and resource name
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Access denials are useful security events when identifiers are protected.

choices.label: Record a validation failure and the rejected field category
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Validation failures can support detection without storing the rejected value.

choices.label: Record a payment failure with a hashed order reference and an allowed masked value such as last four digits
choices.feedbackIfMissed: A minimal, masked record can support investigation without retaining full card or guest data.

choices.label: Attach the full request body to every failure log
choices.feedbackIfSelected: Request bodies can contain personal, financial or authentication data and should not be logged wholesale.

choices.label: Store the authorization header so engineers can replay the request
choices.feedbackIfSelected: Authorization values are secrets and must never be retained for troubleshooting.

hints: Security logs should support detection, not become a duplicate source of sensitive data.
Choose events that preserve a safe identifier, category, resource or masked value rather than a raw request or credential.

feedback.correct: You retained meaningful security events while keeping secrets, raw personal data and full request payloads out of the log.
feedback.incorrect: One or more selected choices either omit useful detection evidence or retain sensitive information unnecessarily.

concept.label: Log security events without logging sensitive values

completion.title: The service can fail without disclosing
completion.message: You protected the client response, kept useful diagnostics value-safe and confirmed the security events that should remain observable.
takeaways: Return generic failure messages to callers and keep implementation detail in protected server-side diagnostics.
Do not log whole request bodies, passwords, tokens, authorization headers or full sensitive values.
Log authentication, access-control and validation events safely so teams can detect misuse without creating a new disclosure path.
